task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-198's implementation: 8 new pure builtin functions (length, lower, upper, trim, contains, startsWith, endsWith, coalesce), a new closed lex-time whitelist mechanism, and call-syntax grammar support added to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex, per the approved design lib/letflow/design/req198-expr-builtin-functions.md. This module is a pure CEL-subset expression evaluator with a hard grep-verified purity contract (moduledoc) that REQ-050's determinism guarantee depends on -- the central thing to independently re-verify is that none of the 8 new builtins, the new {:call, name, args} eval/2 clause, the new tokenizer classification clauses, or the new call-syntax parser clauses introduce any impurity (clock read, Repo, Logger, :rand, :crypto, File, HTTP), and that now()/date_add()/date_diff() were genuinely NOT added to the whitelist (excluded per REQ-197's already-recorded, permanent decision).
acceptance_criteria: Re-run the purity grep yourself against the real file: grep -n "Repo\.\|Logger\.\|DateTime\.\|System\.os_time\|System\.system_time\|HTTPoison\.\|Req\.\|File\.\|:rand\.\|:crypto\." lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex -- confirm zero matches yourself, do not trust the self-report alone.

Confirm @builtin_function_names (and the literal identifier_token/1 / identifier_token_kv/1 mapping clauses) contains exactly the 8 names length/lower/upper/trim/contains/startsWith/endsWith/coalesce and does NOT contain now/date_add/date_diff -- read the code directly.

Confirm no new String.to_atom/1 or String.to_existing_atom/1 call was introduced anywhere in this diff for converting a scanned identifier to an atom (atom-table exhaustion concern from attacker-controlled strings) -- the mapping must be the closed literal 8-clause form.

Confirm eval/2's new {:call, name, args} clause and apply_builtin/2's 8 per-function bodies use only String.*/byte_size/1/pattern-matching primitives (no I/O, no clock, no randomness) -- cross-check against the grep result rather than trusting the design doc's claim alone.

Cross-check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 explicitly, per this project's SECURITY-REVIEWER convention -- state which apply/don't apply and why (this diff touches no migration, no API route, no tenant-scoped table, so INV-1/2/5/6 are expected NOT-APPLICABLE, but verify by diff inspection rather than assuming).

Confirm the ASCII-only case-conversion decision (String.downcase/upcase(s, :ascii)) does not introduce any behavioral security concern (e.g. no injection/normalization-bypass surface, given this module's output only ever feeds a boolean gateway-routing decision, never a rendered/stored value) -- a brief statement is sufficient, this is a low-stakes check for this module's specific use.

Independently run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs yourself -- quote real output, do not trust ELIXIR-DEV's self-report alone.

CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing and confirm 0 new violations.

result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER gate PASS on REQ-198's 8 pure builtin functions and closed lex-time whitelist in lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex. Independently re-ran: purity grep (zero matches), mix compile --warnings-as-errors (exit 0), mix format --check-formatted (exit 0), mix test test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs (148/148 passed), mix letflow.lint_handoffs (0 new violations). Read the real diff end-to-end (not the design doc's paraphrase): confirmed @builtin_function_names is exactly the 8 named atoms via a closed literal 8-clause identifier_token/1 and identifier_token_kv/1 mapping, no String.to_atom/1 or String.to_existing_atom/1 introduced anywhere. Confirmed by direct execution (mix run --no-start) that now()/date_add(a,b)/frobnicate(1) all genuinely fail to parse as {:trailing_input, ...} -- not silently accepted -- while contains(...) parses/evaluates correctly and a wrong-arity call (length(a,b)) safely collapses to false via evaluate_condition/2's catch-false rather than raising. Confirmed contains/startsWith/endsWith use plain String.contains?/2/String.starts_with?/2/String.ends_with?/2 (no Regex, no pattern compilation) -- all 8 builtins are O(n) or O(1), no ReDoS/resource-exhaustion surface. Confirmed the ASCII-only casing/trim decision carries no injection/authorization-bypass risk, since this module's output only ever collapses to a boolean gateway-routing decision within the same pure evaluator, never a rendered/stored/re-interpreted value. Confirmed @unsupported_call_markers has zero diff churn (git diff grep for the attribute name returns nothing). INV-1..INV-8 assessed explicitly: INV-1/2/3/5 NOT-APPLICABLE (no migration/schema/API-route/lookup-by-ID in this diff), INV-4/7 satisfied by absence (no secret handling, no Repo.query anywhere in expr.ex), INV-6 discharged by this report itself, INV-8 satisfied (no bare {:ok,_}= pattern introduced, wrong-arity collapses to false not a crash). Full findings: handoffs/WF02-REQ198-20260830/security-review-req198-findings.md. Routed to REVIEWER via step-02d.
